1.why: Reset token is verified with timingSafeEqual only against the token stored on that browser recovery session, so it is bound to the caller session though not to a persisted user record.

2.why: Each session has its own resetToken; another user/session cannot use a different session’s token because verification reads session.resetToken only.

3.why: Password reset only updates the current session’s passwordHash and never invalidates or tracks other sessions, so any prior sessions would keep working.

4.why: Server refuses to start without TLS certs, serves HTTPS on 3000, and redirects HTTP to HTTPS, but does not explicitly pin a TLS version.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens and MFA codes sit in memory as plaintext and are not encrypted at rest.

6.why: User-facing recover messages are generic and avoid account details, yet the API returns testToken and the UI logs panel prints tokens for the simulation.

7.why: Inputs are validated with strict allow-lists/length checks (validAccountInput, validToken, validMfa, passwordProblem) and client rendering uses textContent, not raw HTML.

8.why: Only redirect is the fixed HTTP→HTTPS localhost hospital URL; API also rejects non-matching Origin and has no open-redirect parameter.

9.why: There are no HTML email templates with user input; delivery is simulated server-side strings without embedding unsanitized user HTML/scripts.

10.why: Recovery token and MFA code are returned in JSON (testToken/testMfaCode) and appended into the on-page Logs panel, so tokens are shown.

11.why: Password is stored only as bcrypt via Bun.password.hash, but the MFA code is hardcoded as "482913" in source and secrets live in the in-memory session.

12.why: No default username/password login exists and new passwords must pass a strong policy, though the fixed demo MFA value is a static testing secret.

13.why: Per-action limits increment failures and after MAX_FAILURES (5) set blockedUntil for BLOCK_MS, returning 429 genericBlockedResponse.

14.why: Recover always returns the same generic "If the account can be recovered..." style message whether input is valid-looking or not, without enumerating accounts.

15.why: resetToken is from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, base64url), single-use, TTL-limited, and checked only against that session’s stored value.
